speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) why written contracts are not mandatory for workers covered under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act; and (b) whether there are plans to make such contracts mandatory.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This covers all workers, whether local or foreign.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers can issue these KETs in the form of an employment contract or employee handbook.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition, for Work Permit holders, employers are required to ensure that their workers receive a copy of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter prior to their departure for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The IPA letter contains key employment information, including occupation, basic monthly salary, and fixed monthly allowances as well as deductions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This requirement is to ensure that before departing their home countries, the workers are already notified of the most critical terms of their employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The requirements to provide written KETs and IPA letters already mean that foreign workers will have sufficient clarity of the details of their employment in written form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There is no further advantage to be gained by requiring employment contracts for foreign workers to be written.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In fact, it will create an unintended outcome that if for some reason no written contract is issued, there is no employment relationship at all and the foreign worker will lose whatever protection he should be entitled to under the law.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would just like to ask whether the Ministry has conducted any studies that look into the extent to which these written agreements between the foreign workers and the employers are actually upheld in the labour market?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: And if there are any violations, for example, are they enforceable and so on?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The concern here is that with the imbalance of power between the foreign worker and the employer, it is possible to push them into doing things which are maybe even illegal or prohibited because they are not aware of their rights and they cannot enforce them effectively, even with these written contracts in place.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Based on a survey of foreign domestic workers in 2015, for example, 94% of foreign domestic workers indicated that they had signed an employment contract with their employers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, in fact, we have got new programmes in place, like the Settling-In Programme (SIP) for both foreign workers and foreign domestic workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We do checks as well as part of the process when they come in, to understand their employment rights as well as advisories on how they can settle in better in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We do a check to make sure that when they come in, they have their IPAs in hand.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, technically, they already have that written contract.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, there is still that remainder, a small minority, which we need to keep on working on.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We do, from time to time, enforce against employment agencies as well as employers who do not comply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On the point of salary reduction, I raised this earlier and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) did say they are reviewing the ability of an employer to reduce the salary after the IPA was issued.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask if there is an update on this review?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The check is, you have to notify the Ministry before you can do it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Of course, if foreign workers have a concern, they can always report to the Ministry and we will take a look at it, for example, if there are other deductions that were not originally agreed to by the employee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Was there a specific area that the Member was after?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that you can do that, but as the other Member had raised, there is a power imbalance here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, if you are offered a salary in the IPA and then you have come to Singapore already, having paid all your deposits back in your home country, and the employer then says, "I am going to reduce your salary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Take it or you go back home", very likely, they will take it and very likely, they will not dare to report to MOM.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The previous reply to me was that 2% of workers faced this problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But with the number of Work Permit holders, 2% actually is quite a big number.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We said 98% of foreign workers came in with IPAs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is something that we can certainly work on.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, the additional mechanism that we have is the SIP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One of the reasons we do that is to ensure that there is that check and balance from the NGO side, trainers, as well as teaching them their rights.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is something that we will continuously improve on.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have given focus to construction, manufacturing and process.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That was where most of our disputes were in the past.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Members have seen, 98% of foreign workers come in with IPAs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But, yes, I do agree that we still have to work on that 2% who come in without IPAs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is something that we hope to expand and we will enforce against employers who do not comply.
